clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old girl with a 10-year history of left recurrent migrainous headaches and ipsilateral intermittent oculomotor nerve palsy presenting with ptosis and diplopia episodes that resolved spontaneously. Brain MRI with contrast performed one year after the last attack revealed an enhancing nodule on the cisternal segment of the left oculomotor nerve, suggestive of schwannoma. Follow-up showed no additional episodes. No histopathological confirmation or detailed neurological examination findings during episodes were documented in the sources.
